tasks.title: New module :data-device-api — contracts, resources, every pure parser
tasks.description: Create the data-device-api Gradle module applying the `library` convention plugin ALONE (no `di`, no Koin dependency — mirroring data-preference-api). commonMain depends on projects.dataCore only. Add include(":data-device-api") to settings.gradle.kts under the data group. Author DeviceId (value class, private constructor, `of()` factory), DeviceCommand (closed sealed set: Screencap/WmSize/WmDensity/GetProp/EmuAvdName), DeviceResource/DeviceStateResource/AvdResource/AvdName/ToolProbe/ToolKind/DeviceInfoResource/MirrorFrame/TransportStats, the DeviceCommandExecutor/AdbHostSource/EmulatorSource/MirrorTransport interfaces, EVERY pure parser (parseAdbDevices, parseWmSize, parseWmDensity, parseAvdList, trimToPngSignature), buildDeviceArgv/buildHostArgv, probeCandidates, MirrorTuning, and DeviceCommandException. No core/ directory — nothing here is internal. This placement is what makes AC-2/AC-3/AC-41/AC-42/AC-44 testable with no phone attached (AS-7).

acceptanceCriteria.text: settings.gradle.kts includes ":data-device-api" under the data group.

DeviceId has a private constructor; `of()` is the only mint point outside parseAdbDevices.

No core/ directory exists in the module; the module has zero platform-specific source sets.

tasks.title: New module :presentation-feature-mirror — the Orbit state machine
tasks.description: Create presentation-feature-mirror applying `feature` + `di`; add include(":presentation-feature-mirror") under the presentation-feature group. Dependencies mirror presentation-feature-settings minus projects.presentationCoreNavigationApi (and minus compose.material3 unless MirrorContent needs a Material3 composable directly); commonTest adds libs.kotlinx.coroutines.test. Files: source/mirror/{MirrorContract,MirrorViewModel,MirrorHost,MirrorContent}.kt — MirrorHost replaces the usual *Screen because no Destination exists for this shell-slot surface (document the deviation in the module's CLAUDE.md). core/picker/PickerNavigation.kt (nextSelectableIndex: skips non-selectable rows, clamps at both ends) and core/stats/StatsFormatter.kt (formatStatusLine) as internal pure helpers. di/PresentationFeatureMirrorModule.kt. MirrorViewModel owns the polling gate (discovery PAUSES while a session streams), flatMapLatest session switching, PNG decode on Dispatchers.Default via decodeToImageBitmap(), a public StateFlow<ImageBitmap?> held OUTSIDE Orbit state, and a 1s stats ticker. No ByteArray-bearing type ever enters MirrorUiState.

acceptanceCriteria.text: MirrorUiState never carries a MirrorFrame/MirrorFrameModel field; frame pixels live only in the separate StateFlow<ImageBitmap?>.
Discovery polling pauses while session is streaming and resumes when the session ends.
Session switching uses flatMapLatest so rapid Start/Stop never leaves two capture loops alive.
The entry point is named MirrorHost, not MirrorScreen, and the module CLAAUDE.md documents why no Destination/navigation.md checklist applies.
Arrow/Enter intents never carry isMetaPressed semantics (ownership split from RectifyWindow's Cmd+1/2/3 handler).
`./gradlew :presentation-feature-mirror:build` succeeds.

references.ref: presentation-feature-settings/ (four-file Orbit shape and feature+di build.gradle.kts block to mirror, minus navigation-api)

tasks.expectedOutput: A new Orbit MVI feature module with MirrorHost/MirrorViewModel/MirrorContract/MirrorContent and the two pure helpers, ready for compose-application to inject and for T-13's tests.
tasks.hypothesis: Keeping pixels in a StateFlow outside the reducer and stats on a separate 1s ticker stops every future annotation feature from inheriting a reducer pass per frame at up to 10fps.

tasks.title: MEASURE the real v1 capture rate and latency — the gate decision 9 demands
tasks.description: With a real device attached (local toolchain, not CI), run the desktop app and record over a 60-second session: achieved fps (from TransportStats, not a stopwatch), mean and p95 per-frame capture round-trip, mean decode time, dropped-frame count, and observed end-to-end latency via a wave test (a running stopwatch on the device against the mirror). Record device model, screen resolution and link type (USB 2/3, wifi). Also time one frame end-to-end with the dot grid visible vs covered, to settle the PRF-1 suspicion. Set MirrorTuning.CaptureFloorMs from the measurement rather than keeping the 100ms default unexamined, and write the numbers plus the re-flagged NFR-1 waiver into the delivery notes. AN ESTIMATE IN THIS SLOT FAILS THE TASK — the number must be measured, never carried forward from the brainstorm estimate (3-7fps/250-500ms).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Delivery notes contain a real measured fps and per-frame latency number, with device model, resolution and link type recorded alongside.
MirrorTuning.CaptureFloorMs is either justified against the measured number or left at 100ms with a written reason, not silently unexamined.
Frame time is measured with the StageSurface dot grid visible vs covered by MirrorFrameView, settling the PRF-1 suspicion one way or the other.
The NFR-1 waiver is restated in the delivery notes as flagged-for-re-review-before-ship, per the Stage 1 gate's option-B answer.

tasks.expectedOutput: A real, recorded fps/latency measurement with its conditions, and a justified (or explicitly deferred) MirrorTuning.CaptureFloorMs value.
tasks.hypothesis: Screenshot polling delivers roughly 3-7fps/250-500ms per the brainstorm estimate, but that number must be replaced with a measurement before the slice can be called done (decision 9 is a gate, not a nicety).
definitionOfReady: T-4 merged (capture loop exists)
T-11 merged (MirrorViewModel and TransportStats plumbing exist)
A local adb and either a USB-debug device or one installed AVD are available (demo/measurement only, never required for CI).
definitionOfDone: The delivery notes contain real numbers, not an estimate, or the task fails.
The NFR-1 waiver is restated as flagged-for-re-review-before-ship.
outOfScope: Automated test coverage of the measurement itself (there is no CI harness for this, by design)
